hints.title: Like Percentage Ratio
hints.text: Calculate the like percentage as likes divided by the sum of likes and dislikes.

hints.title: Avoid Integer Truncation
hints.text: Multiply likes by one point zero or cast to float before division to preserve decimal precision.

hints.title: Filter Strictly Under 60%
hints.text: Add a condition that the ratio is strictly less than zero point sixty and order by problem identifier ascending.

hints.title: Complete Query
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT
    problem_id
FROM Problems
WHERE likes * 1.0 / (likes + dislikes) < 0.60
ORDER BY problem_id ASC;
```

complexity.time: O(P log P) where P is the number of problems
complexity.space: O(P) for sorting result problem identifiers
complexity.notes: Direct arithmetic filter and sort on problem_id.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Integer division in SQL can truncate decimals to zero.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle division precision and sort problem_id ascending.

import pandas as pd

def low_quality_problems(problems: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    cond = (problems['likes'] / (problems['likes'] + problems['dislikes'])) < 0.60
    return problems[cond].sort_values(by='problem_id')[['problem_id']]
